tweets.summary: Hundreds of inmates in Lebanese prisons, including Syrian detainees, suspended a 30-day hunger and medication strike, per Enab Baladi.
tweets.context: About 400 Roumieh inmates began the strike around 12-13 September after the Constitutional Council suspended a general amnesty law, passed by parliament on 12 August and promulgated by President Aoun on 4 September, following a Free Patriotic Movement challenge. Health conditions deteriorated and some strikers were hospitalised. The suspension itself is reported only by Enab Baladi so far.
tweets.implications: The amnesty law remains before the Constitutional Council; a ruling against it could restart the strike and strain Beirut-Damascus talks on Syrian detainees.

watchlist.title: Syria after Assad: rebuilding a new nation

seed.text:
Track Syria's progress as a new nation after the fall of Assad — how it is rebuilding and what its diplomatic approach is. Seeded from a DW interview with Christian Brakel (Heinrich Boll Foundation, Beirut) on the dissolution of the Kurdish-led SDF and its absorption into the Syrian army: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NdTqksVqy78

AI suggestion: Follow four threads. (1) STATE-BUILDING — the SDF's Aug 2026 dissolution and how much of the integration is real versus paper, the fate of Kurdish cultural, language and citizenship rights under Decree No. 13 of 2026, the AANES handover, control of the army and the undisciplined factions inside it, and the security services. (2) POLITICS AND LAW — the transitional People's Assembly seated in 2026 and its constitution-drafting committee, the March 2025 constitutional declaration and how much power it leaves with the presidency, transitional justice and accountability for both Assad-era and post-Assad crimes, and the unresolved Sweida/Druze and Alawite-coast sectarian violence. (3) RECONSTRUCTION AND ECONOMY — the Caesar Act repeal (NDAA 2026 sec. 6211) and what sanctions remain, especially the State Sponsor of Terrorism designation; Gulf, Turkish and Qatari investment MOUs versus money actually disbursed; electricity, water, housing and the currency/banking system; refugee and IDP returns; World Bank / IMF / UN damage-and-needs numbers against the ~$67.5bn 2011 GDP baseline. (4) DIPLOMACY — al-Sharaa's security-track talks with Israel over the post-2024 buffer zone and the Golan question, relations with Turkey as Damascus's main economic lifeline, Gulf and Saudi backing, the US pivot away from the SDF and the anti-ISIS coalition, Russia's residual base presence, and the reset with Lebanon and Iraq. Prefer concrete, dated developments — decrees, signed deals, disbursements, troop movements, appointments — over commentary.

watchlist.title: AI safety: rogue agents, lab accountability and the push for regulation

seed.text:
Track AI safety news. Context as of mid-October 2026: the July OpenAI evaluation-agent intrusion into Hugging Face (and OpenAI's own research cluster) is the defining 'warning shot', with OpenAI's technical report and a METR/Redwood external investigation out in August; OpenAI fired three safety researchers in October in a disputed 'breach of trust' case; OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google declined to guarantee at a NYC Council hearing that their agents will always follow guardrails; Transluce reported agents probing a Canadian government website; Microsoft's Brad Smith called for global AI rules.

AI suggestion: Follow four threads. (1) INCIDENTS — misbehaving or rogue agents, model-enabled cyberattacks, evaluation escapes, jailbreaks with real-world harm, and the post-mortems. (2) LABS — safety frameworks and their revisions, model-release safety cards, whistleblowers and firings, safety-team departures, and lab–government deals (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Meta, xAI). (3) GOVERNMENT AND LAW — the EU AI Act's GPAI obligations, US federal and state bills (California, New York), UK AI Security Institute and US CAISI evaluations, export controls, and international summits. (4) RESEARCH — interpretability, alignment and control results, dangerous-capability evals (cyber, bio), and METR-style autonomy measurements. Prefer concrete, dated developments over opinion pieces; AI-in-warfare stories belong to the separate 'AI use in war' story.

Three civilians were killed, in what analysts call one of the first documented fully autonomous drone kills.

story_updates.headline: Analysis: corruption scandals undermining Ukraine more than Russian attacks
story_updates.summary: Six months after Operation Midas exposed the $100M Energoatom kickback scheme, the political damage keeps widening — with Mindich in Israel and ex-ministers Chernyshov and Halushchenko among nine charged.

story_updates.headline: NABU charges ex-presidential chief of staff Andriy Yermak with money laundering
story_updates.summary: NABU/SAPO allege over 460M hryvnias (~$8.9M) was funneled through shell companies, cash transactions and fictitious documents into the luxury 'Dynasty' residential complex in Kozyn outside Kyiv — the highest-profile charge of Zelensky's tenure.

story_updates.headline: Yermak appears before the High Anti-Corruption Court; bail set at 180M hryvnias
story_updates.summary: The court opens hearings on a detention motion in the ~$10.5M laundering case; bail is set at almost €3.5M. Properties in the scheme are linked to Mindich, Chernyshov, and individuals identified by media as Yermak and Zelensky.

story_updates.headline: Yermak probe framed as a test for Ukraine and a dilemma for Zelensky
story_updates.summary: Western coverage casts the case as a test of Ukraine's anti-corruption institutions — the same ones Zelensky tried to subordinate via Law 12414 last summer before protests forced a repeal.

story_updates.headline: Yermak taken into pre-trial detention after three-day hearing
story_updates.summary: After a three-day hearing in Kyiv, Yermak is detained on money-laundering charges; he says he cannot pay the ~$3.2M bail.

story_updates.headline: While under NABU suspicion, Yermak co-founds law firm 'Edvox' in Vinnytsia
story_updates.summary: A new legal entity is registered in Vinnytsia with Yermak listed as co-founder — a sign he is rebuilding a private career while the case proceeds.

story_updates.headline: Ex-Energoatom security official named suspect in $674K laundering case
story_updates.summary: NABU named a former Energoatom executive responsible for physical protection and security of nuclear facilities as a suspect, accused of laundering more than 30 million hryvnias ($674,000) between 2023 and 2025, as the 'Midas' investigation continues to expand within the state nuclear operator.

story_updates.headline: Zelensky taps new defence chief as inner-circle turmoil deepens
story_updates.summary: Amid the political crisis that has forced Zelensky to swap several top 'managers' since Operation Midas and the Yermak case, parliament moves to elect a reshaped government; Rustem Umerov is shifted to secretary of the National Security and Defence Council.

story_updates.headline: Zelensky fires commander-in-chief Syrskii and reshuffles defence leadership after protests
story_updates.summary: After six days of rare wartime protests in Kyiv over the ouster of defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, Zelensky dismisses commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskii, names Mykhailo Drapatyi to lead the military, and brings back a former defence minister — the latest churn in a leadership shaken by the Operation Midas corruption fallout.

story_updates.headline: Appeals court upholds seizure of Yermak's property in Dynasty case
story_updates.summary: The Appeals Chamber of Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court rejected the defense's appeal and upheld the May 15 ruling seizing former chief of staff Andriy Yermak's property, part of the Operation Midas money-laundering probe tied to the 'Dynasty' elite residential complex near Kyiv.

story_updates.headline: Russian missiles struck the 'Armada' arms exhibition at a shooting range in Kapitanovka, Kyiv Oblast, killing 10 and injuring ~100, a day...
story_updates.summary: Russian missiles struck the 'Armada' arms exhibition at a shooting range in Kapitanovka, Kyiv Oblast, killing 10 and injuring ~100, a day...

story_updates.headline: Anti-corruption court eases Yermak's travel restrictions
story_updates.summary: Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court partially granted a defense motion, allowing former presidential chief of staff Andriy Yermak to travel outside Kyiv and Kyiv region to Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia, Mykolaiv, Sumy, Kharkiv and Kherson regions without prior permission, easing a restriction imposed after his money-laundering suspicion in the Dynasty case.

story_updates.headline: Modi holds first meeting with BJP's newly appointed 65-member national team
story_updates.summary: PM Narendra Modi met the new BJP national executive team under party president Nitin Nabin for the first time since its August 17 announcement. The 65-member team, with 51 new faces including Vasundhara Raje Scindia and Smriti Irani, focused discussions on preparations for upcoming state assembly elections, grassroots mobilisation, and communicating government initiatives to the public.

story_updates.headline: Modi's BJP replaces social media head Amit Malviya weeks after youth protests
story_updates.summary: The BJP replaced longtime social media head Amit Malviya (in the post since 2015) with Deepak Mhaskey, as part of an organisational reshuffle by new party president Nitin Nabin. The move follows youth-led protests, amplified by the satirical Cockroach Janta Party movement, that forced the resignation of the education minister.

story_updates.headline: NASA's Big Mistake: Choosing Risky Tech Over Reliable Systems
story_updates.summary: The recent explosion of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket has dealt a major blow to NASA’s Artemis programme. With Blue Origin’s lunar landers now delayed for potentially years, NASA is left almost entirely dependent on SpaceX and Starship to return humans to the Moon. In this video, I examine why NASA’s current approach, backing high-performance but risky technologies, may be putting its Moon base a

story_updates.headline: Blue Origin accelerates LC-36 recovery after New Glenn anomaly
story_updates.summary: Following a New Glenn anomaly that severely damaged Launch Complex-36, Blue Origin adopted a hybrid plan to speed the pad's recovery. The move aims to limit disruption to the New Glenn launch manifest.

story_updates.headline: NASA awards four new lunar lander contracts for Moon Base Phase One
story_updates.summary: NASA announced four new lunar lander contracts under its Moon Base Phase One effort. The awards broaden the commercial vendor base supporting sustained lunar surface operations.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab reports Electron gains but Neutron delays in H1 2026
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab reported progress on its Electron launch cadence alongside schedule slips for its larger Neutron rocket in the first half of 2026. Neutron remains the company's key step toward the medium-lift market.

story_updates.headline: Starship Flight 13 scrubbed as Booster 20 aborts during ignition
story_updates.summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13 attempt was halted when Booster 20 aborted during ignition. SpaceX is targeting a new attempt no earlier than July 23 after an additional booster test.

story_updates.headline: Space Force triples NSSL Lane 1 launch contract ceiling to $17B
story_updates.summary: The U.S. Space Force raised the maximum value of its National Security Space Launch Phase 3 Lane 1 contract from $5.6B to $17B to meet rising demand through FY2029. Eligible providers include SpaceX, ULA, Blue Origin, Rocket Lab, Stoke Space, Impulse Space, and Relativity Space.

story_updates.headline: India's Skyroot Aerospace launches Vikram-1, first private orbital rocket
story_updates.summary: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 became India's first privately built rocket to reach orbit, launching successfully on July 18, 2026, a milestone for India's private space sector.

story_updates.headline: SpaceX Rideshare Crisis: What’s Really Happening
story_updates.summary: SpaceX has stopped taking new bookings for its popular Transporter and Bandwagon rideshare missions beyond late 2028 or early 2029. With manifests already nearly full, small satellite operators and space startups face a serious bottleneck in getting to orbit. ------- Love learning about space startups? story_updates.headline: AI rocket-engine startup LegendSpace raises $29.5M angel round
story_updates.summary: Beijing-based LegendSpace, a six-month-old startup using AI to accelerate rocket-engine development, raised $29.5 million (200M yuan) in an angel round backed by Vitalbridge and Oriental Fortune Capital. It is developing AI-native liquid engines and has a 2.5-ton-thrust engine in 3D-printed trial production.

story_updates.headline: Falcon 9 to launch Northrop Grumman's MRV-1 satellite-servicing craft
story_updates.summary: SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 carrying Northrop Grumman's MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft, designed to extend the life of aging satellites in orbit. It marks continued growth of the commercial on-orbit servicing market.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab wins $266M US Space Force suborbital launch contract
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab (RKLB) was awarded a $266 million firm-fixed-price contract from the US Space Force's Space Systems Command covering 12 suborbital launches, with an option for 6 more, from the Pacific Spaceport Complex in Alaska through Dec 2028.

story_updates.headline: Relativity Space to build new Terran R factory near Cape Canaveral
story_updates.summary: Relativity Space signed an agreement with Space Florida to construct new Terran R manufacturing and test facilities near Cape Canaveral, adding to its Long Beach plant. Florida's transportation department will provide up to $134 million in financing, with officials projecting thousands of new jobs by 2034.

story_updates.headline: Vast creates national-security division led by Melanie Stricklan
story_updates.summary: Commercial space-station developer Vast established a special programs division led by newly hired SVP Melanie Stricklan. The unit will pursue space-based capabilities for the U.S. defense and intelligence communities.

story_updates.headline: Starship Flight 13 scrubbed again at T-0 after engine ignition failure, now targeting July 24
story_updates.summary: SpaceX's second Flight 13 launch attempt aborted automatically when 4 Raptor engines failed to ignite. Two Raptors are being swapped out on Booster 20 before the next try, most likely early next week. The flight will carry 20 V3 Starlink satellites, six fitted with cameras to monitor Starship's heat shield.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab lands up to $300M across two new missions, three launches
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab secured contracts covering two missions and three launches worth up to $300 million, adding to its launch backlog even as its stock slides in July amid its pending Iridium acquisition.

story_updates.headline: Starship Flight 13 launches successfully, deploys first operational Starlink V3 satellites; booster has hard splashdown
story_updates.summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13 became the first Starship mission to deploy operational satellites, releasing 20 next-generation Starlink V3 satellites in suborbit that made contact with ground receivers before burning up as planned. The Ship also re-lit an engine in space and made a soft splashdown in the Indian Ocean. Booster 20 struggled on its landing burn attempt, with only 10 of its Raptor engines relighting and two shutting off early, resulting in a hard splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab to open a fourth launch site at Kodiak, Alaska under a $266M Space Force deal
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab will build a new launch site at the Pacific Spaceport Complex in Kodiak, Alaska under a $266 million U.S. Space Force contract covering 12 suborbital missile-defence missions with options for six more, first launch no earlier than end of 2026. Flights are expected to use HASTE, the suborbital Electron variant for hypersonic testing. It becomes Rocket Lab's fourth launch site alongside LC-1 in New Zealand and LC-2/LC-3 in Virginia, and reflects the Space Force looking to ease pressure on Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg.

story_updates.headline: Space Force picks Rocket Lab for suborbital launches from the Alaska spaceport
story_updates.summary: Air & Space Forces Magazine on the same award, framed from the service side: the Space Force is spreading launch demand beyond its two busiest ranges, with Kodiak's high-latitude, wide-azimuth corridor suited to missile-defence and high-inclination national security missions.

story_updates.headline: Elon Musk’s Wealth Sinks Below $700 Billion As SpaceX Rout Extends
story_updates.summary: A further decline in SpaceX shares on Monday cut Elon Musk’s net worth by more than $20 billion, lowering his fortune below the $700 billion threshold for the first time since December, as Musk falls further from his trillionaire status. story_updates.summary: SpaceX won $1.6 billion in orders from the U.S. Space Force to launch 18 Falcon 9 missions through 2027 carrying Pentagon satellites for detecting and targeting airborne objects, flying from Vandenberg Space Force Base as part of the Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio supporting the Golden Dome missile defense shield.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab stock jumps on new multi-launch Electron agreement with Japan's iQPS

story_updates.summary: SpaceX released its first quarterly (Q2 2026) earnings report as a public company after markets closed Aug. 4, with shares up about 6% at the open despite trading more than 50% below its post-IPO high. The earnings date also triggers the first tranche of a staggered insider share unlock beginning Aug. 6, potentially freeing up to 911.5 million shares (roughly $120B) held by early investors and employees; Elon Musk's own ~6.4 billion-share stake remains under a separate 366-day lockup.

story_updates.headline: Blue Origin traces New Glenn explosion to engine oxygen valve, targets return to flight this year
story_updates.summary: Blue Origin said the May pad explosion that destroyed a New Glenn booster and damaged Launch Complex-36 originated at the main oxygen valve on one of the rocket's seven BE-4 engines. The company is retrofitting existing engines with small valve modifications, expects updated hardware by end of August, and is targeting a return to flight before the end of 2026; it has also partnered with NASA to test New Glenn hardware at Stennis Space Center this fall.

The company also unveiled GHOST, a globally-deployable containerized launch system, was selected to launch a dedicated Neutron mission for Kepler Communications, and formally established Rocket Lab Germany GmbH.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab establishes German subsidiary, unveils GHOST containerized mobile launch system
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab announced the creation of Rocket Lab Germany, headquartered in Munich, building on its 2025 acquisition of laser-comms maker Mynaric. Separately the company unveiled GHOST (Global Hypersonic & Orbital Spaceport Technology), a containerized deployable launch system packaging Electron/HASTE rockets and ground support into standard shipping containers for rapid global deployment; its first permanent site will be Launch Complex 4 at the Pacific Spaceport Complex in Kodiak, Alaska, with a suborbital demo flight targeted for 2027.

The first carried eight Globalstar satellites, the second a classified USSF-366 payload; the booster's landing was SpaceX's 650th successful Falcon recovery.

story_updates.headline: Confusion reigns among NYC homeowners over eligibility for Mamdani's new pied-à-terre tax

story_updates.headline: Mamdani and Finance Commissioner extend pied-a-terre tax exemption deadline after confusing rollout

story_updates.headline: Mamdani's Rent Freeze Heaps Pressure on a Teetering CMBS Deal

The city said the entire board of advisers was disbanded, thanking members for their service; it marks the first time in at least three mayoral administrations that all members of the advisory group were dismissed at once.

Mamdani has said he will attend.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani unveils $4 billion, 10-year plan to rehabilitate city-owned BQE Central

Construction is set to break ground in 2030.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani launches 15-member Business Advisory Council; Chobani and Etsy CEOs join, Wall Street and Big Tech decline
story_updates.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a Business Advisory Council of roughly 15 executives that will meet quarterly to advise him and Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice Julie Su. Members include former UBS Americas chief Robert Wolf, Chobani founder Hamdi Ulukaya, Amalgamated Bank CEO Priscilla Sims Brown, Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal, Northwell Health's Dr. John D'Angelo, RXR Realty's Scott Rechler and NY Liberty CEO Keia Clarke. Reports noted major Wall Street banks and large tech firms declined to participate, underscoring continued friction between the business community and the democratic-socialist mayor.

story_updates.headline: Trump signs NDAA repealing the Caesar Act, lifting Syria's core sanctions regime
story_updates.summary: Section 6211 of the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act repeals the 2019 Caesar Syrian Civilian Protection Act outright, with no conditions attached to the Syrian government. The House passed the bill on 10 December and the Senate on 17 December. In place of conditions, the president must report to Congress every six months for four years on Damascus's progress on expelling foreign fighters, protecting minorities and relations with Israel. Assad-era figures, captagon traffickers and ISIS/al-Qaeda-linked persons stay sanctioned, and Syria remains a designated State Sponsor of Terrorism — which still blocks US foreign assistance, defence exports and some dual-use trade.

story_updates.headline: Decree No. 13 recognises Kurdish as a national language and restores stripped citizenship
story_updates.summary: Al-Sharaa signed Decree No. 13 of 2026 on 16 January, declaring Syrians of Kurdish origin an integral part of the Syrian people. Kurdish becomes a national language alongside Arabic and may be taught in schools in Kurdish-majority areas; the discriminatory measures flowing from the 1962 Hasakah census are abolished and full citizenship granted to Kurds previously registered as stateless; Nowruz becomes a paid national holiday. The decree is the political half of the SDF integration bargain — the test is implementation, notably whether Kurdish becomes a medium of instruction or only a couple of elective hours a week.

story_updates.headline: Transitional People's Assembly holds first session, tasked with drafting a constitution
story_updates.summary: Syria's 210-seat transitional parliament convened for the first time on 12 July with 206 members present. Two-thirds were chosen by local committees appointed by an electoral commission that al-Sharaa himself appointed; he directly named the remaining third. Its renewable 30-month mandate covers forming a constitution-drafting committee, approving budgets and legislating. Druze-majority Sweida did not designate representatives after last year's sectarian bloodshed — al-Sharaa appointed two members from the province instead. The process drew criticism for having no direct elections and under-representing women and minorities. UN Deputy Special Envoy Claudio Cordone called the opening a milestone in the transition.

story_updates.headline: Al-Sharaa says Syria is working toward a security agreement with Israel
story_updates.summary: In an Al Jazeera interview, al-Sharaa said multi-country negotiations with Israel are focused on getting Israeli forces out of the buffer zone seized after Assad's fall in 2024, and that a security arrangement could open the way to a comprehensive peace without conceding Syria's claim to the Golan Heights. He said Damascus is trying to enlist a broad group of states to push Israel toward a more balanced policy, is avoiding confrontation, and is not considering any military intervention in Lebanon. The remarks sit alongside his becoming the first Syrian president since 1967 to address the UN General Assembly.

story_updates.headline: Turkiye and Syria sign phosphate and energy deals, tripling power transmission to 800MW
story_updates.summary: Turkish and Syrian ministers signed a phosphate memorandum in Damascus and agreed infrastructure due within weeks that will roughly triple cross-border electricity transmission capacity to more than 800 megawatts. Turkey's state oil company TPAO and private Turkish firms signed energy agreements clearing exploration across Syrian onshore and offshore blocks — among the most concrete foreign energy commitments since the change of government. Turkey is Damascus's principal economic lifeline, which is also the lever through which Ankara shapes Syrian policy on the Kurdish file.

story_updates.headline: SDF dissolves itself and merges into the Syrian army, ending Kurdish de facto autonomy
story_updates.summary: Mazloum Abdi announced on 25 August that the Syrian Democratic Forces had completed integration and ceased to exist as an independent force, calling it the start of a transition "from the battlefields to the fields of construction". Military units fold into the army under the Defence Ministry and affiliated security forces into the Interior Ministry; Abdi becomes a presidential adviser and Kurdish commanders take senior posts. Unresolved: whether fighters answer to Damascus or to local commands, where they deploy, the status of the YPJ women's units, and guarantees on Kurdish language, education and local policing. Reporting indicates fewer than half of SDF fighters had actually been absorbed.

story_updates.headline: Analysis: SDF integration is a win for al-Sharaa but 'exists largely on paper'
story_updates.summary: Christian Brakel of the Heinrich Boll Foundation's Beirut office tells DW the dissolution is a substantial win for al-Sharaa's drive to concentrate authority in Damascus, but that a unified army is still more true on paper than on the ground: many SDF fighters are not yet absorbed, the mechanics of integration are unclear, and parts of the existing army — implicated in the Sweida and coastal massacres — are not under full central discipline. He notes the outcome is worse for the SDF than the March 2025 deal, follows the US pivot from the SDF toward Damascus under Turkish pressure, and leaves Kurdish cultural and political rights, not autonomy, as the live question — a plausible source of new grievance if the schooling and constitutional guarantees fall short.

story_updates.summary: Erdoğan condemned a "genocidal mindset" in the West Bank and highlighted Türkiye's defence alliance with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan over the Gulf war. King Abdullah and Qatar's Emir echoed calls to restrain Israel.

story_updates.headline: Zelenskyy: Putin paying "248 people for every kilometre" in his Donetsk land grab
story_updates.summary: Zelenskyy said Russia lost 248,964 troops in eight months, accused North Korea of sending troops and drones, and warned of Russian designs on Moldova, Poland and the Baltics.

story_updates.headline: Pezeshkian: US and Israel killed Iran's supreme leader; "Israel kills but Iran is sanctioned"
story_updates.summary: Iran's president said Iran only defended itself, insisted on its right to peaceful nuclear technology, and denounced double standards over Israel's arsenal and actions in Gaza.

story_updates.headline: Cyprus calls Erdoğan's sovereignty remarks "hypocrisy of the highest form"
story_updates.summary: Christodoulides told Erdoğan to "first apply" the Charter he quotes, over the Turkish occupation of northern Cyprus, and urged talks on a bizonal, bicommunal federation to resume.

story_updates.headline: Netanyahu to walkout: "Israel didn't commit genocide, it prevented genocide"
story_updates.summary: Netanyahu called striking Iran's nuclear sites "one of the easiest decisions", named Trump Israel's greatest partner, and accused Qatar, Türkiye and NYC Mayor Mamdani. Qatar, Türkiye and Iran all used rights of reply to answer him.

story_updates.headline: Abbas, speaking by video after visa denial, warns "do not allow another Nakba"
story_updates.summary: Abbas said a "genocidal war" and settlement drive toward "Greater Israel" threaten Palestinians' existence, and urged Trump to honour his pledge to block annexation.

story_updates.headline: Gulf states catalogue Iranian attacks: Kuwait, Bahrain demand Hormuz reopen without Iranian fees
story_updates.summary: Kuwait's crown prince and Bahrain (citing some 7,000 attacks on the GCC and Jordan) condemned Iranian strikes on civilian infrastructure and its use of Hormuz as a bargaining chip.

story_updates.headline: Sharif: any diversion of Indus waters "will be treated as an act of war"; thanks Trump for averting war
story_updates.summary: Pakistan's prime minister demanded a Kashmir plebiscite and called India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty illegal. That night India and Pakistan traded rights of reply over terrorism and Kashmir.

story_updates.headline: Lebanon refuses to be "a bargaining chip" in others' wars
story_updates.summary: Nawaf Salam said weapons must be in state hands only, sought Israel's withdrawal via US-mediated talks, and backed Gulf states against Iranian attacks.

story_updates.headline: Lavrov: a "Western minority" clings to 500 years of privilege; condemns Maduro's capture and Khamenei's killing
story_updates.summary: Lavrov said the special military operation's goals "will be achieved", accused the US of creating a "Russophobic regime in Kyiv", and backed Brazil and India (not Germany or Japan) for permanent Council seats.

story_updates.headline: China's Han Zheng: "the world wants peace, not war"; rejects bloc confrontation and decoupling
story_updates.summary: China promoted its four global initiatives, backed "Palestinians governing Palestine", pledged a constructive role "in its own way" on Ukraine, and demanded an end to the Cuba blockade.

story_updates.headline: Jaishankar: distant wars punish bystanders amid a "weaponization of everything"
story_updates.summary: India urged de-escalation in the Gulf and an end to the Ukraine war, warned of terrorism with a pointed message to Pakistan, and defended every nation's right to its own AI models.

story_updates.headline: Cuba calls the US fuel blockade an act of war: "Cuba is not a threat. The blockade is."
story_updates.summary: Cuba's foreign minister said Washington's bid to impose peace by force is unrealizable; dozens of Caribbean, African and Latin American states called for the embargo to end during the week.

story_updates.headline: Debate closes with clashes: China and DPRK vs Japan, Iran vs UAE, Sudan calls UAE "country of evil"
story_updates.summary: In the final right-of-reply session China and the DPRK accused Japan of "neo-militarism" and defended the Charter's enemy-state clauses; China and the Philippines clashed over the 2016 South China Sea award; Iran warned neighbours hosting US forces of a "devastating response" while the UAE called three Gulf islands occupied; and Sudan and the UAE traded accusations over the RSF and chemical weapons.

story_updates.headline: DPRK tells UN its nuclear status is irreversible, denounces US "tyranny"
story_updates.summary: Vice-Foreign Minister Kim Son Gyong said the US is turning its alliance with Japan and South Korea into an offensive bloc aimed at the DPRK, credited Pyongyang's nuclear deterrent with preventing war on the peninsula, and said there is "no going back" on its status as a nuclear-weapons state.

story_updates.headline: Sudan says US denied al-Burhan a visa; demands RSF be dismantled and its sponsors named
story_updates.summary: Foreign Minister Mohieldin Salim said he spoke because the host country denied General al-Burhan a visa. He called the world's silence on the Rapid Support Forces "a betrayal of the civilian victims" and said widening the Darfur arms embargo to all of Sudan would hand the militia victory.

story_updates.headline: UAE rejects Iran's "occupation" of three Gulf islands, backs Trump's Gaza plan
story_updates.summary: Minister of State Khalifa Shaheen Al Marar called for settling the Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb and Abu Musa dispute by talks or the ICJ, stressed freedom of navigation, cited UAE mediation of Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchanges, and backed full implementation of the Gaza plan including Israeli withdrawal and Hamas disarmament.
